proposed.text: A contractor specifies XHHW wire for the main feeder of an office building. What is the primary advantage of XHHW over THWN for this application?

options.text: XHHW is cheaper and lighter, reducing installation labor costs and overall project expenses.
XHHW has cross-linked polyethylene insulation offering superior thermal stability and durability for high-load applications
XHHW can be installed without conduit, unlike THWN which requires a raceway, simplifying installation.
XHHW can carry 25% more current than THWN at the same wire size due to better heat dissipation, enhancing efficiency.

proposed.rationale: XHHW uses cross-linked polyethylene insulation, providing superior durability and thermal stability compared to THWN's thermoplastic coating. This makes XHHW preferred for main feeders and high-load circuits that generate sustained heat. [A]: Incorrectly suggests cost and weight advantages, when XHHW is actually more expensive than THWN. [C]: Confuses installation method; both THWN and XHHW are typically installed in conduit. [D]: While ampacity may differ by size, the advantage isn't a blanket 25% increase; it stems from better thermal properties.
proposed.explanation: Incorrectly suggests cost and weight advantages, when XHHW is actually more expensive than THWN. Confuses installation method; both THWN and XHHW are typically installed in conduit. While ampacity may differ by size, the advantage isn't a blanket 25% increase; it stems from better thermal properties. XHHW uses cross-linked polyethylene insulation, providing superior durability and thermal stability compared to THWN's thermoplastic coating. This makes XHHW preferred for main feeders and high-load circuits that generate sustained heat. XHHW's cross-linked polyethylene provides superior insulation durability, preferred for feeders and heavy-load circuits.
